deities: Goddess Bilai Mata (Vindhyavasini, a form of Durga)

history.period: CONFLICT (verify): one news source says 12th century with a 500–600-year-old idol; a tourism source says ~250 years old
history.summary: Ancient and famous temple in Dhamtari city, dedicated to the self-manifested (swayambhu) idol of Maa Vindhyavasini, worshipped as 'Bilai Mata' — 'bilai' meaning cat, because legend says wild cats sat around the stone where the goddess emerged. Local tradition recounts that King Narhar Deo, hunting in a dense forest, found his horses halted near the stone; water began to flow from the spot, and the goddess appeared in his dream ordering worship at that place, after which the idol emerged from the earth. Devotees believe the black idol is still slowly rising. The temple has a red-sandstone structure with old-style wall carvings, a divine stepwell in the premises, and a daily single ghee flame (two during Navratri, when Jyoti Kalash is installed). NOTE: animal sacrifice of 108 goats during Navratri, said to date from King Narhar Deo's reign, was abolished around 1938 and replaced with raw pumpkin offering. One source calls it one of five Shaktipeeths of Chhattisgarh — unverified.

name: Bilai Mata Mandir
town_description: Dhamtari is a city and the administrative headquarters of Dhamtari district in central Chhattisgarh, about 76 km south of Raipur. It lies on the banks of the Mahanadi and is known as a temple town, with the Rudri pick-up weir (1912–15) and the Gangrel (Ravishankar) reservoir nearby. Mahatma Gandhi first visited Dhamtari in 1920 during the canal agitation, giving the region a place in India's freedom movement. The city is surrounded by forests and the Sihawa hills, and its temples — Bilai Mata, Rudreshwar Mahadev at Rudri and Maa Angarmoti — draw pilgrims year-round.
